newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dollar, debt futures seesaw on data.
newsitem.headline: Australian dollar, debt futures seesaw on data.

text.p: The Australian dollar and debt futures seesawed after official data showed a 1.3 percent private sector rise in the final first quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) report.
Market analysts had been looking for an outcome of below 1.0 percent growth to keep slim hopes of a further easing monetary policy on the agenda.
However, the overall final AWOTE was revised down to 1.0 percent after the 1.3 percent seen in the premlinary data reported earlier this month.

The dollar eased to US$0.7832/37 after firming briefly from US$0.7835/40 where it stood just before the data was released at 0130 GMT, while the June 10-year bond futures contract wavered either side of its pre-data 92.255.
First quarter company profits were released at the same time, falling 3.4 percent compared with an expected 2.0 percent fall and after the 8.6 percent rise in the December quarter.
